templates.name: Anaerobic power — Beginner four-week reference
templates.purpose: Give the workout-generation model an exercise-based progression reference for anaerobic power, not a mandatory athlete program.

selection_rules.use: Select methods matching the athlete's sport demand, environment, equipment and level; preserve the category objective and weekly progression shape.
selection_rules.avoid: Do not include every listed method, invent a method, progress multiple loading variables at once, or use fatigue as proof of effectiveness.
selection_rules.session_order: Complete relevant preparation first; perform speed, power and high-skill work before fatiguing strength or conditioning; place low-priority capacity work later.
selection_rules.dose_application: The weekly prescription applies to the primary_reference method. Preparation and supporting references use their own released method-dose compatibility; they must not inherit the primary dose blindly.

templates.prompt_reference_text: Anaerobic power — Beginner four-week reference. Approved method candidates: Cycling Sprint Repeats. Use this as a flexible exercise-based planning reference: Week 1 (entry and establish baseline): primary reference dose 4 sets/series × 6s at near maximal, with 90s recovery. Week 2 (accumulate successful exposure): primary reference dose 5 sets/series × 6s at near maximal, with 120s recovery. Week 3 (highest development exposure): primary reference dose 6 sets/series × 6s at maximal quality, with 120s recovery. Week 4 (consolidate and reduce fatigue): primary reference dose 3 sets/series × 6s at near maximal, with 90s recovery. Progress only after acceptable technique/output, readiness and schedule checks; otherwise repeat or regress. Week 4 consolidates rather than automatically overloading. Apply dose only to the primary reference method; supporting methods retain their own approved dose.

templates.prompt_reference_text: Repeated high-intensity ability — Beginner four-week reference. Approved method candidates: Repeated High-Intensity Cluster. Use this as a flexible exercise-based planning reference: Week 1 (entry and establish baseline): primary reference dose 2 sets/series × 4x10m at 90-95%, with 20s reps/3min sets recovery. Week 2 (accumulate successful exposure): primary reference dose 2 sets/series × 5x10m at 90-95%, with 20s/3min recovery. Week 3 (highest development exposure): primary reference dose 3 sets/series × 4x10m at 95%, with 20s/3min recovery. Week 4 (consolidate and reduce fatigue): primary reference dose 2 sets/series × 4x10m at 90%, with 25s/3min recovery. Progress only after acceptable technique/output, readiness and schedule checks; otherwise repeat or regress. Week 4 consolidates rather than automatically overloading. Apply dose only to the primary reference method; supporting methods retain their own approved dose.
